exposure: oxytocin use (in women with prior C-sections)
cohort: The study included 13 cases of complete uterine rupture identified among 10,447 deliveries at the Local Health Unit of Tamega e Sousa, Portugal, between 2019 and 2024.
finding: Uterine rupture occurred in 12.44/10,000 deliveries, predominantly in women with prior caesarean sections, with no maternal deaths but 7.7% perinatal mortality.
mod_finding: Uterine rupture was predominantly observed in women with prior caesarean sections, and caution is advised regarding oxytocin use in this group.
